data.text:
Claims family on apply — landed on branch wt/claims (worktree .claude/worktrees/claims). Not committed.

New file: internal/job/apply_claims.go — applyClaimed, applyClaimExpired, applyHeartbeat, and applyReleased relocated out of apply_tasks.go (name and applyTable entry unchanged). Tests in internal/job/apply_claims_test.go, plus driveClaimsFamily + TestApplyDeterminism_ClaimSequenceRebuildsIdentically in apply_determinism_test.go.

Handlers moved onto commit(): RunClaim (--force breadcrumbs stay in the payload; flipFocusOnClaim still runs after the commit), RunRelease (note-then-release pair, both emitted), RunHeartbeat (body split into heartbeatInTx), and expireStaleClaims / expireStaleClaimsInTx. maybeExtendClaim now emits a `heartbeat` event through the caller's batch instead of moving claim_expires_at silently.

Post-release status: nothing derived, and no new payload key. This cache has no 'blocked' status — blockedness is a row in `blocks` that readers derive — so released and claim_expired both write 'available' unconditionally, as RunRelease and expireStaleClaims already did.

Read-time expiry: still a read verb that writes, unchanged behavior, but now guarded by a cheap SELECT EXISTS so a read with nothing stale opens no transaction and writes no local.json. Only when something is stale does it run a real commit() batch of claim_expired events.

labels.go and criteria.go (the relations leaf's files) still open their own transactions, so their four handlers get a batch via a new `batchInTx(tx)` in envelope.go plus `b.persist()` after their commit, under a TODO(relations leaf) comment. Four small edits per file; the auto-extend tests for label add/remove would otherwise have to be deleted.

Behavior changes: (1) an auto-extend now records a heartbeat event, visible in `job log` — documented in docs/content/docs/concepts/leaves-and-claims.md; (2) applyHeartbeat stamps updated_at, so a label add by the claim holder now bumps updated_at where it previously did not.

Pre-existing defect found, NOT fixed: `job list` never sets ListFilter.Actor (cmd/job/list.go), so the claim_expired a read verb sweeps is recorded with an empty actor. Verified end to end. It predates this leaf and spans several read verbs; it wants its own leaf.

Verification: go fix/gofmt/go vet/go mod tidy clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; go build ./... clean; node --test internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs 421/421. Red confirmed first: 8 of 10 new tests failed before the implementation.

data.note: Integrated. Post-release status needs no payload key: blockedness is derived from the blocks table, so released and claim_expired always write available. maybeExtendClaim now emits a heartbeat through the caller's batch; labels.go and criteria.go get a batchInTx until the relations leaf moves them onto commit, and that helper must go with them because it builds the recorder inside an open SQLite transaction. Pre-existing defect the agent found and left: `job list` passes no actor to the expiry sweep, so a read-time claim_expired carries an empty actor; it wants its own issue.

data.text:
Relations, criteria, provenance and kind are on apply, on branch wt/relations (worktree .claude/worktrees/relations). Not committed.

New files: internal/job/apply_relations.go (blocked, unblocked, labeled, unlabeled, found_in_set, found_in_cleared, kind_changed), internal/job/apply_criteria.go (criteria_added, criterion_state), internal/job/apply_relations_test.go. applyTable in apply.go gains nine entries, added as one block so the claims agent's edit to the same map does not collide.

Handlers moved to commit(db, func(tx, b)): RunBlockMany, RunUnblockMany, RunLabelAdd, RunLabelRemove, RunAddKind's inline labels, RunAddCriteria, RunSetCriterion, RunSetFoundIn, RunClearFoundIn, RunSetKind, and RunImport's whole Phase B. recordBlocksUnblockedOn / recordBlocksUnblockedOnCancel are replaced by one emitBlocksUnblockedOn(tx, b, blockerID, blockerShortID, reason, actor) in blocks.go; close.go and cancel.go call it, and the DELETE moved into applyUnblocked. No handler in the family calls recordEvent; the only remaining callers are claims.go and heartbeat.go (agent-claims').

Import's batch order: per task in pre-order DFS created -> labeled -> criteria_added; then every blocked event walking `flat` in document order; then every found_in_set. Both ends of a block therefore exist before the edge event. dbIDByParsed is gone: the events carry short ids, so nothing needs a row id except planNewCriteria.

Payload additions: CriterionEntry gains `sort_key` (apply must not mint a fractional key or a shuffled log reorders criteria), and its `short_id` is now filled by every writer. UnblockedPayload.Reason is now a typed UnblockReason with UnblockManual / UnblockBlockerDone / UnblockBlockerCanceled; the JSON strings are unchanged. Marshalling sample updated. No other JSON key changed.

Two writers had to split read from write, because apply's writes are idempotent and so cannot report what changed: labels.go gained splitLabelsByPresence (added vs existing, removed vs absent) and criteria.go replaced insertCriteria with planNewCriteria (validates, mints short id + sort key, writes nothing) and SetCriterionState with ResolveCriterion (read-only). RunUnblockMany's "not blocked by" check is now an explicit EXISTS rather than RowsAffected. criteria_test.go's four low-level tests were rewritten onto RunAddCriteria/RunSetCriterion — the functions they called no longer exist, by design.

Also fixed in passing: blocks.created_at, task_labels.created_at and found_in.created_at came from SQLite's strftime default (wall clock at insert); they now come from the event ts, and applyDump was widened to carry all three so a clock-reading apply is visible. That widening is what caught mutation 2 below.

Determinism: TestApplyDeterminism_ImportedPlanRebuildsFromAShuffledLog imports a plan with labels, criteria, a cross-ref blockedBy and a foundIn, then sets two criterion states, removes a label, unblocks one edge by hand, changes a kind and closes a blocker (auto-unblocking two edges) — shuffle, rebuild into a fresh database, dump-compare. TestApplyDeterminism_ImportedPlanRebuildsFromItsEventsAlone is the plain criterion: import once, rebuild from the events, identical. TestApplyDeterminism_RelationsFamilyRebuildsIdentically does the same over the handler-driven sequence, and TestRelationsHandlers_EmitPositionedEventsOnly fails on any events row with rep '' after that sequence.

Red first: the new test files failed to build on the missing UnblockManual and CriterionEntry.SortKey. Mutation-checked with two injected bugs — applyCriteriaAdded minting its own sort key (caught by the unit test) and applyLabeled stamping created_at from the clock (caught by the determinism dumps only after applyDump was widened; before that it survived, which is why the widening is part of this change).

Verification: go fix (two passes, clean), gofmt, go vet, go mod tidy, go build all clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; node --test internal/web/jstest/*.test.mjs 421/421. Driven end to end against a freshly built binary: block/unblock, label, criteria + --criterion on done, kind, found-in, import with blockedBy and foundIn — 0 rows with rep '' and the blocks table emptied by the close.

Left for agent-claims: RunLabelAdd/Remove, RunAddCriteria and RunSetCriterion still call maybeExtendClaim inside the batch, unchanged and with its old signature. It writes claim_expires_at directly, so a claim held while labelling still produces a state change no event describes.

data.title: Read-time claim expiry from job list records an empty actor
data.description: `job list` never sets ListFilter.Actor (cmd/job/list.go), so when the read-time expiry sweep fires from `list` the claim_expired event is recorded with an empty actor; `job log` shows "claim expired @". status, orient, next, closed tail and issueroot all pass the actor through. Found by the claims apply leaf (eZF00) on 2026-09-01. Matters more now that the event is positioned and replicated. Fix: thread the resolved identity into list's filter like the other read verbs, with a regression test on the recorded actor.

data.text:
The store landed on branch wt/store (worktree .claude/worktrees/store). Not committed.

New files: internal/migrations/0011_log_watermarks.sql, internal/job/store.go (open-time sync, watermarks, bootstrap), rebuild.go (replay + rekey rewrite + collision detection + RunRebuild), reconcile.go (the three repair rules), rekey.go (RunRekey), cmd/job/rebuild.go, cmd/job/rekey.go, plus store_test.go, reconcile_test.go, rekey_test.go, cmd/job/rebuild_test.go.

SEQ AGREEMENT. commit() now takes eventlog.AcquireLock(cachePath) around the whole span, primes the recorder from appender.LastSeqLocked() (a new one-line addition to eventlog: LastSeq takes the lock and would deadlock inside it), applies as events are emitted, appends with AppendLocked BEFORE tx.Commit, asserts each returned Seq equals the minted one (a mismatch rolls the transaction back), then advances log_watermarks in the same transaction. So the seq comes from the file, not MAX(seq) in the cache — which matters because purge erases event rows and the cache's seq has holes the file does not. newRecorder/persist became newRecorderLocked/persistLocked because UpdateLocalState takes the same lock; commit must never nest (flock is per open file description).

ON OPEN. Hot path: a stat per file against log_watermarks; equal everywhere and no unknown file, done. A rep whose events the cache holds but whose file is missing is bootstrapped from the cache (gapless run only, else a notice and no rebuild) — that covers both this repo's own pre-store history and, unexpectedly, `job merge`, which stages a copy of the other cache with no store beside it. Fresh clone: no watermarks, files present, rebuild. Foreign file grew: rebuild + reconcile. Legacy (any rep '' row): never rebuild, one-line notice, own writes still append and apply.

A DESTRUCTIVE CASE THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME. "Rebuild whenever sizes disagree" wipes any cache whose watermarked file is absent — it replays less than the cache holds. Found by the merge tests: RunMerge stages the other .jobs.db in a temp dir with no .jobs/ beside it, and the first version of this leaf silently emptied it. Fixed by the bootstrap-any-missing-rep rule above, plus a fourth state, StoreIncomplete ("log incomplete"), which refuses to rebuild and says so when a file cannot be written back.

REKEY. The doc says the mapping applies "from its position in the order". It cannot: the event a rekey exists to disentangle is the `created`, which is always earlier, so a positional fold would leave the collision and the rebuild would still fail. applyRekeys is therefore a pre-pass over the whole ordered stream, rewriting e.Task and every exact-match string inside the payload for that replica. Deterministic on every machine, so both caches dump identically (tested).

RECONCILE. Two deviations. (1) The claim repair emits TWO events, not one: a `released` for the loser (actor `reconcile`, payload gains Reason "lost-merge" and LostClaim, the loser's position string) and a `claimed` re-establishing the winner — releasing alone would leave the task unclaimed, which is not "the earlier one wins". (2) The re-establishing claim's envelope actor is the WINNER, not `reconcile`: applyClaimed reads the holder from e.Actor. LostClaim is what makes the repair idempotent across later rebuilds; both the close and the claim rules are tested for that.

ALSO CHANGED. eventlog.Appender opens its file lazily on first append — it used to create an empty file at OpenAppender, so every read verb that ran an empty commit() left a tracked zero-byte log file. `job status` gains a Store line in md and json ({replica, files, events, cache}). openDBFromCmd and findAncestorDB now accept a directory that has .jobs/log and no cache, which is what makes a fresh clone work on the first command. Two test harnesses had to move each side of a merge into its own directory: the store is the .jobs/ beside the cache, so two caches in one directory shared one log and one replica id.

VERIFIED. go fix/gofmt/vet/mod tidy clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; go build clean; node --test 421/421. Red confirmed first (11 undefined symbols, then three reconcile rules failing on behaviour). Driven against a copy of this repo's real .jobs.db: 2,772 legacy rows survive, its one positioned event bootstraps into a log file, a foreign file dropped in prints the notice and changes nothing, `job rebuild` refuses, and a new `job add` still works. Eight parallel `job add` processes produce a gapless 8-line log and 8 tasks.

data.note: Integrated. Facts for adopt and cursors: commit() holds the store lock across recorder, append (AppendLocked, seq primed from the file) and the SQLite transaction, and sets log_watermarks in the same transaction. syncStore in store.go runs on every OpenDB: in sync, rebuilt, "predates the store" (any rep '' row; never rebuilt), or "log incomplete" (a replica's file missing and not writable back). Rekey is a whole-stream pre-pass. StoreSyncOf(db) gives job status its line. Appender opens its file lazily so read verbs leave no empty file.

data.text:
Adoption landed on branch wt/adopt (worktree .claude/worktrees/adopt). Not committed.

New files: internal/job/adopt.go (probe + orchestration), adopt_commit.go (verify, append, swap), adopt_translate.go (legacy rows -> envelopes, cache -> snapshot payload), apply_snapshot.go, dump.go (dumpCache/dumpHistory — logicalDump lifted out of merge_test.go), adopt_test.go. Changed: internal/eventlog/envelope.go (+Legacy), internal/job/apply.go, database.go (OpenDB calls adoptIfLegacy before it opens anything), local.go (+AdoptFailed), gitignore.go, cmd/job/gitignore.go, gitignore tests, DOCS.md, docs/reference/setup.md, docs/getting-started/initialize.md.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, and where it aborts: open the legacy cache (outside the lock, because openCache's config seed takes the lock and flock does not nest) -> take the store lock -> re-probe the path (another process may have adopted) -> mint the replica id if local.json has none -> translate every rep '' row into a `legacy` envelope with ts = created_at*1000 -> mint one `snapshot` envelope -> assign rep/seq from appender.LastSeqLocked -> build <cache>.adopting from the existing log plus those envelopes -> DUMP BOTH AND COMPARE. That is the abort point: any difference removes the candidate, writes the diff to <cache>.adopt-failed, appends nothing and renames nothing. Only then: append the lines, write the watermarks into the candidate, persist local.json, close both, rename <cache> -> <cache>.pre-adopt (sidecars too) and <cache>.adopting -> <cache>.

THREE FINDINGS THE BRIEF DID NOT PREDICT, all found by driving a copy of this repo's real database.

1. THE SNAPSHOT CANNOT GO LAST. The brief says ts = now, after everything. That silently breaks the cache: this repo's log already holds 25 positioned lines whose tasks were created by LEGACY events, so with the snapshot last those lines apply to a task that does not exist yet and their event rows get task_id NULL — `job log` and `job show` lose them. The snapshot's ts is therefore min(existing line ts) - 1: it summarizes the legacy history, which is what a snapshot is for, and everything the log already holds replays on top of it. Those lines' effects are already in the payload and every apply writes absolute values, so replaying them lands on the same state — and the dump comparison is what proves that rather than assuming it. With no existing lines (the ordinary case) the snapshot is last, as the brief describes.

2. applySnapshot CANNOT TRUNCATE `tasks`. events.task_id REFERENCES tasks(id) with no cascade, so emptying tasks fails the foreign key for every event already recorded against a task, and re-inserting could not restore the link because an event row does not carry the short id it was resolved from. Tasks are reconciled instead: upsert by short id (which keeps every row id, and so every event's link), then delete any task the snapshot does not name along with its events — exactly purge semantics. The other five tables are truncated and refilled as the brief says. `events` is untouched.

3. LEGACY EVENT ROWS ARE LINKED AFTER THE FACT. Their task is created by the snapshot, which is later in the order, so rebuildFromInTx records them with insertEventRowID and sets task_id at the end of the replay from the row id it got back. Deferring the whole row to the end (the obvious alternative) reorders `job log` within a second.

Also worth knowing: adoption is NOT fatal when it aborts — the legacy cache still works exactly as it did, and blocking every command on a conversion would be an outage. The refusal is printed and recorded as adopt_failed in local.json so the next open does not rebuild and compare the whole database again. JOBS_NO_ADOPT=1 reads a legacy database as-is for one invocation; that is what makes the `job log` byte-identity evidence possible.

One known, transitional imperfection in `job log` order: main still writes some rep '' rows (claims.go and heartbeat.go), so this repo's database has legacy rows interleaved with positioned ones inside the same second. A legacy row's ts is its created_at in whole seconds, so it now sorts before a positioned row from the same second whatever their row ids were. Two lines of 3,160 move, both within their own rendered minute. It cannot happen once no writer emits unpositioned rows.

Verification: go fix/gofmt/go vet/go mod tidy/go build all clean; go test ./... -p 1 green; node --test 421/421. Red confirmed first (11 undefined symbols). Mutation-checked with three injected bugs: applySnapshot dropping completion_note (caught), dropping a label's created_at (caught), and removing apply's legacy short-circuit (SURVIVED — the rebuild has its own path for legacy envelopes and never calls apply on them, so TestApply_LegacyEnvelopeWritesNoState was added to exercise that rule directly; it now catches it). Driven end to end against a consistent copy of this repo's database with a freshly built binary: 2,776 legacy events carried across, a snapshot of 465 tasks, 0 rows with rep '', `job status` says "cache in sync" on the first and second open, `job rebuild` now succeeds where it used to refuse, and `job add` works.

data.note: Integrated as f79885a. Two corrections to the plan worth keeping: the snapshot sorts immediately before the earliest line the log already holds, not last, because positioned lines written before adoption name tasks whose created events are legacy; and applySnapshot upserts tasks by short id rather than truncating, because events.task_id references tasks without ON DELETE. JOBS_NO_ADOPT=1 reads a legacy cache without converting it; a failed adoption is recorded in local.json (adopt_failed) with the diff at .jobs.db.adopt-failed so it is not retried on every command.

data.text:
Cursors are on the log position on branch wt/cursors (worktree .claude/worktrees/cursors). Not committed.

NAME. One word everywhere: `position`. Go keeps `eventlog.Position` and gains `EventEntry.Position()`; the API adds a `position` field beside `id` on every event; the query params are `?since=<position>`, `?at=<position>` and `/log?before=<position>`; the SSE `id:` line is the position, so a browser's Last-Event-ID is usable verbatim as ?since=; the island is `{headPosition, eventCount}` (was `headEventId`); `--at` on scripts/replay-snapshot takes a position; the JS calls it `position` too (`frame.position`, `xToPosition`, `positionToX`, `stepPosition`, `windowForPosition`, `parseAtFromQuery` returns one).

LEGACY CURSORS. position.go now accepts an empty rep, and `EventEntry.Position()` puts the cache row id in the seq slot for a legacy row ("<ts>--<rowid>"). Documented in position.go as meaningful only within one cache. This is not academic: this repo's own database is entirely legacy, so every cursor the dashboard exercised in the browser pass was of that form.

SQL. `job.EventPositionExpr(alias)` / `EventPositionArgs(p)` are the one place the (ts, rep, CASE WHEN rep='' THEN id ELSE seq END) tuple is written; every ordering and bound uses it, so SQL and Go agree on the legacy substitution. Ordering everywhere moved off (created_at, id) onto the tuple — the log query, the actors walk, the actor page's event list, /log's newest-first sort.

ORDINALS, NOT POSITIONS, IN THE FRAME CACHE. replay.mjs's FrameCache answers "how far apart are these two frames", which a position cannot answer, so a Frame now carries both `position` (the cursor) and `ordinal` (events since genesis) and the cache keys on the ordinal. The buffer holds one array ordered by position plus a position→index map; `frameAt(cursor)` resolves an unknown cursor by binary search to the newest event at or before it, so a bookmarked ?at= survives events arriving around it. `reverseEvent` cannot know the previous event's cursor (that is a fact about the ordered log, not the event) so it leaves position null and _replayBackward refills it.

A REAL BUG THIS FOUND, unrelated to cursors but fatal to them. Assets are content-fingerprinted, so `import … from "./position.mjs"` resolves against the importer's hashed URL and 404s; the layout's importmap is what maps unhashed specifiers onto fingerprinted URLs. A module missing from that map kills the whole graph downstream of it with ZERO console errors — `sleepy load` said 0 errors while the scrubber silently never entered history mode; `sleepy wire` showed the 404. Added internal/web/templates/importmap_test.go, which scans every relative import under assets/js and fails when one has no entry (red on position.mjs, and every pre-existing module was already covered). Gotcha recorded.

RED FIRST, with one exception I should name: position.mjs was written before its test file, so those 9 JS tests were green on the first run. Every other new test was watched fail first — the eventlog Legacy tests (undefined symbol), the four internal/job cursor tests (undefined GetEventsAfterPosition), the three handler tests (400 on a position ?at=), and the importmap test (position.mjs missing).

VERIFIED. go fix / gofmt / vet / mod tidy clean; `go test ./... -p 1` green; `go build ./...` clean; `make test-js` 431/431. Browser: served a copy of this repo's store on :7841 and loaded /, /plan, /log, /actors, /issues plus each of those under `?at=1788309934000--2833` — all 200, zero console errors, 40 resources with no non-200, one fetch (/events?limit=2772). The scrubber enters history from the URL and its banner reads "?at=1788309934000--2833 · 1h ago · 2026-09-02 00:45:34"; /log renders 500 live rows with zero duplicate positions; an SSE frame's `id:` line is the position; `job tail --format=json` frames carry it.

NOT DONE, deliberately. `internal/job/search.go`'s note search still orders by e.id DESC — that is a display ordering, and after a rebuild row-id order equals position order, so it is stable either way. Same for merge_snapshot.go's read of the legacy events table.
